QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_18

question.text: Per the 2019 Bain & Company philanthropy report referenced in Chapter 2, the estimated annual funding gap for meeting only 5 of the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in India by 2030 is approximately:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 2.2.2(A), 'this translates into a funding gap of about Rs. 4.2 lakh crore annually for meeting only 5 of the 17 SDGs by 2030'. 4.2 lakh crore = Rs 4,20,000 crore = approximately USD 50 billion at 2019 exchange rates. India accounts for over 20% of the world performance gap in 10 of the 17 SDGs. The Trap: Option A is 10x too low. Option C (4.2 crore) is six orders of magnitude off. Option D (2.1 lakh crore) is exactly half, a common arithmetic slip. Cross-Exam Context: X-A/X-B (IA) and V-A (MF Distributor) reference philanthropy/CSR market sizes. XII (SMF) treats India macro-financial data. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Sizing talk aside, SIAs use this 4.2 lakh crore figure in the 'materiality of sector gap' paragraph of a SAS-100 limited-assurance report — it frames why even a Rs 10 crore ZCZP issue is 'material in a resource-scarce sector'.
